I've been farming this same land for 25 years. My body isn't what it was, and my son works in the city now, so it's just me and my wife. I can't do everything by hand anymore. I hire machinery for planting and harvesting. I stick to what I know works here in Quzhou.

**Wheat (planted October, harvested June):**
All 4.5 mu goes to wheat in winter, same as always. I'll use the certified variety from the township supply cooperative — not some fancy new thing, just the one that's done well here for years. I spread compound fertilizer before rotary tilling, then topdress with urea at jointing. Three irrigations: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. I do two sprays — one herbicide early, one fungicide later when powdery mildew starts showing up, which it always does.

**Maize (planted June, harvested September):**
Right after wheat harvest, I plant maize on the same 4.5 mu. I always use hybrid seed — everyone does now, the yield difference is real. I topdress heavily at the big bell stage. Summer rains help, but I'll irrigate at silking if it's dry — that's the stage where skipping water costs you. One herbicide spray early, maybe one more if insects show up bad. I use rotary tillage quickly after wheat to get seeds in the ground fast. Every day late in June costs yield.

I won't change much this year. At my age, I'm not experimenting.
